title: Bending-Active Metal Panel Deformation
summary: My individual thesis connects target geometry, opening patterns and elastic sheet behaviour.

credits.research: JosHsuan Chao - individual thesis research and computational design
credits.media: Bending-Active Metal Panel Deformation project imagery.

overview.introduction: A research story about geometry, openings and the behaviour of a metal sheet.

form.label: FORM
heading: The shape begins
with an opening.
paragraphs: A desired surface is only the beginning. This thesis asks how the geometry of a cut pattern can help a metal sheet take that form.
Miura folding represents the surface’s local angles. Those angles link the overall shape to a repeatable operation at the scale of one opening.
form.aside: A relationship between design intent and material behaviour.

system.label: SYSTEM
heading: From angle
to pattern.
paragraphs: I developed an individual thesis workflow connecting Miura representation, a regression-based opening library and dynamic physical simulation.
The opening values inform a reconstructed mesh. Paired edges then describe how the openings close and the panel bends.
system.footnote: The source workflow, shown here as documentary evidence.

pattern.label: SYSTEM / DETAIL
heading: A local rule.
A different surface.
paragraphs: The research relates opening length and width to bending angle through a sampled function library.
Arc, twist and saddle mock-ups explore how those local relationships accumulate into different surfaces.
pattern.note: The opening-pattern library links sampled dimensions with bending angle; the physical studies explore that relationship across several surface types.

make.label: MAKE
heading: Sewn into
space.
paragraphs: Pairs of holes and plastic ties close the patterned openings. Panel connections, including rivets, bring the separate sheets into a spatial prototype.
The joints remain visible: the method becomes part of the object’s expression.
make.note: Two people assembled the spatial prototype over three days.

validation.label: EVIDENCE
heading: From simulation
to the made object.
paragraphs: I compared simulated forms with physical mock-ups and brought the patterned panels together in a spatial installation. The assembled prototype made the relationship between openings, seams and curvature tangible.
The digital model lets the surface, connections and assembled form be examined together.
validation.note: The available evidence does not establish structural certification or universal prediction accuracy.

credits.label: RESEARCH / REFLECTION
heading: Intent,
translated.
credits.summary: Target geometry, local opening rules and physical prototyping become one connected design workflow.
credits.contribution: I developed this individual thesis at National Cheng Kung University under the supervision of Prof. Kane Yanagawa. I combined Miura-inspired surface representation, an opening-pattern library, linear regression and dynamic physical simulation to connect target geometry with the deformation of metal panels.
credits.collaboration: Arc, twist and saddle studies led to a spatial prototype assembled collaboratively from patterned panels.
credits.limitation: Geometry inspection only. No structural analysis or fabrication validation runs in the browser.
